title: The full media path: direct upload, event-driven processing, CDN reads
caption: Object storage is both the landing zone for uploads and the origin behind the CDN.

steps.text: The uploader asks the API for a URL; the API records a pending row.
The uploader PUTs the bytes straight to the store with the presigned URL.
ObjectCreated lands on a queue; transcoders read the raw file, write each rendition back to the store, and mark the row ready.
Viewers read through the CDN. Only misses reach the store, so a video watched 1M times is fetched from the origin about once per edge.

scenarios.name: Transcoder crashes
scenarios.summary: A transcoder dies mid-job: the event is redelivered and another worker redoes it. Renditions go to fixed keys, so the redo overwrites instead of duplicating.

steps.text: ObjectCreated for v_77 reaches a transcoder.
The worker crashes halfway through the 1080p rendition, before it acks the event.
After the visibility timeout, the queue hands the event to another transcoder.
It writes v_77/1080p.mp4 again (same key: an overwrite) and marks the row ready. The half-done output never became visible, because a PUT is all or nothing.

scenarios.name: Risk: no CDN
scenarios.summary: Viewers read the store directly: every view pays egress and 20–100 ms to first byte, and one viral video can exceed the request rate a single key supports.

steps.text: Uploads and processing work exactly as before.
Every view is a GET on the store: 1M views of a 50 MB clip is 50 TB of egress, paid at origin prices, and each viewer waits for the first byte from one region.
A video goes viral: tens of thousands of GETs per second on one key, above what one prefix serves, so the store answers 503 Slow Down.
Mitigation: put a CDN in front with the store as origin. The edges absorb repeat views, and the store sees roughly one fetch per edge.

scenarios.name: Viral miss storm
scenarios.summary: A brand-new viral video is in no edge cache yet, so thousands of simultaneous misses reach the origin at once. Request coalescing or an origin shield collapses them into one fetch.

steps.text: A video is shared widely seconds after it's marked ready; viewers everywhere request it at once.
No edge has it cached, and each edge server misses separately: thousands of origin fetches for the same object.
Mitigation: the CDN coalesces concurrent misses for one key into one origin request, and an origin shield (a mid tier) means only that tier talks to the store.
After the first fetch, views are edge hits and the store is quiet again.
